deckTitle: Hilfe, ich bin ein Mensch! — Human Nature Science Wrestling
verdict: The source deck and the crown jewel of the corpus — every major mechanic in the Kayfabizarro system traces its DNA back here. Named strength: the mechanics DON'T describe the science, they PERFORM it — Non-Violent Resistance stops the game to change a rule, The Scissors physically destroy a card forever, The Stag Hunt literally only activates through cooperation. Named weakness: five die-modifier cards (Protopia, Loneliness, Vagus Nerve, Egalitarianism, The Commons) cluster at G3 because a number adjustment cannot carry the intellectual weight of a Margulis or an Arendt — each deserves a social mechanic, not a stat tweak. Table-ready: YES — and uniquely so, because this deck requires no prior genre knowledge to play, only a willingness to be human.
blurb: 56 science cards that make evolutionary psychology, social neuroscience, and philosophy of cooperation playable at any table. For educators, facilitators, and curious humans who want to argue about human nature without reading a textbook.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — Extraordinary comic-book splash: animals playing cards surrounded by floating science concept previews (Mirror Neurons, Oxytocin, Loneliness, Homo Economicus), UFOs, and FrizzleBob chaos — every inch advances the deck thesis
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'HILFE, ICH BIN EIN MENSCH!' in massive yellow Bangers font is the most instantly compelling title in the corpus — existential, bilingual, comic-book-scale
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — The cover IS the deck performed: animals enacting cooperation and social breakdown simultaneously while the scientific concepts hover as playable mechanics above them
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — No other card game cover looks remotely like this; underground comix aesthetic fused with academic science textbook in a genuinely singular composition
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — Maximum 'what IS this?!' energy — the density of concepts, the FrizzleBob chaos, and the bilingual title guarantee a double-take every time
coverQA.coverNote: Strongest cover in the corpus. 'HILFE, ICH BIN EIN MENSCH!' screams like a philosophy text having a panic attack — and every concept previewed on the cover is a mechanic you'll actually play. If this doesn't make someone pick it up, nothing will. BLÖDSINN! this cover is perfect.

notes: Source deck — the Hilfe, ich bin ein Mensch! comic is the origin material from which the entire Kayfabizarro project was derived. Simultaneously a game artifact and the project's theoretical foundation. Cover tagline 'Science is a Wrestling Match' is the most concise description of the project's animating principle available anywhere. The Artifact card categories (Connection, Peace, Power, Childhood, Philosophers, Future) appear as section headers but are not labeled on individual cards — taxonomy is invisible when decks are shuffled. Page 2 is a manifesto/intro page, not a card page. Page 17 contains four blank Cut-and-Play card templates. The KAYFABIZARRO card (54) is the only card in the corpus that names and defines the game system it exists within. Academic reference list embedded in cards spans Darwin, Dawkins, Margulis, Hobbes, Rousseau, Bregman, Tomasello, Ostrom, de Waal, Christakis, Pariser, Turkle, Thaler, Rosa, Arendt, Kant, Fromm, Buber, Gandhi, Rushkoff, and more — a reading list as a card game. sourceFile 'Help_I_Am_A_Human - ADD web.pdf' not found in folder at time of re-analysis; cover QA performed from standalone cover PNG in SLIDE DECKS folder; card data carried from prior 18-page ADD.pdf analysis.

urgent: LONELINESS (card 23): '-1 to Quest Die' is the weakest mechanic for the strongest public health data in the deck. The lore ('as deadly as 15 cigarettes a day') demands a social mechanic — e.g., all other players must ignore the Loneliness player for one round.

EGALITARIANISM (card 40) and THE COMMONS (card 16): Both produce mass card draw without social activation. Graeber/Wengrow and Ostrom citations deserve conditional mechanics — e.g., Egalitarianism requires the player with the most cards to agree.
quickWins: PROTOPIA (card 49): '+1 to the Die roll' is correct philosophy, minimal table impact. Reframe as '+1 to the Die, and name one specific thing that is better than yesterday' — the declaration makes it a card.
THE VAGUS NERVE (card 07): Die reset to 3 is clean but bodyless. Consider: 'Reset the Quest Die to 3. Take a breath. No card may be played for 10 seconds.'
RESONANCE (card 30): Vibe amplification requires Emotional Contagion to have set a Vibe first. Either make explicit or give Resonance a standalone activation condition.
niceToHave: The Artifact card categories (Connection, Peace, Power, Childhood, Philosophers, Future) are only visible in section headers. Adding a one-word category tag to each card face would make the taxonomy portable when decks are shuffled.
THE NUDGE (card 28): 'Influence without forcing' needs a table-executable definition. Consider: 'Whisper a suggestion to the next player. If they follow it, both draw a card.'
Blank Cut-and-Play page (page 17): Consider a companion guide on integrating custom cards into play.

cards.power: Sympathy Instinct: Play to cancel a "Selfish" action.
cards.lore: Sympathy will have been increased through natural selection. (Ref: Darwin)
cards.gradeReason: Canceling a Selfish action is precise and thematically exact but requires a Selfish action already in play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian naturalist illustration. Subject: tortoise writing field notes, watching two animals share food without noticing. Mood: careful observation.

cards.power: Ego Boost: Gain control of the narrative, but isolate your Actor.
cards.lore: We are survival machines—robot vehicles blindly programmed. (Ref: Dawkins)
cards.gradeReason: Narrative control at the cost of social isolation is the Dawkins thesis made mechanically irresistible and personally punishing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical scientific diagram. Subject: hamster in a top hat examining its own reflection, spotlight on it, everyone else turning away. Mood: sovereign loneliness.

cards.power: Symbiosis: Combine two Scene cards into one stronger card.
cards.lore: Life did not take over the globe by combat, but by networking. (Ref: Margulis)
cards.gradeReason: Physically merging two Scene cards enacts symbiosis at the table — the deck is literally rewritten.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: biological watercolor. Subject: gecko and flower fused at the root, glowing where they join, growing larger. Mood: productive merger.

cards.power: Domestication: Turn an enemy card into an ally.
cards.lore: Evolution favors those who can get along. (Ref: Hare & Wrangham)
cards.gradeReason: Converting an enemy card mid-play is the thesis of the entire deck distilled to one mechanical action — evolution happens in this turn.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: before-and-after evolutionary diagram. Subject: snarling wolf on left panel, golden retriever on right, same animal. Mood: selective warmth.

cards.power: Reflection: Copy the Effect/Power of the last card played.
cards.lore: Why I feel what you feel. Intuitive communication. (Ref: Bauer)
cards.gradeReason: Power-copying is mechanically strong but 'Reflection' underserves the neuroscience concept it should embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: neuroscience illustration. Subject: two monkeys in berets at a glass wall, both making the same gesture simultaneously, surprised. Mood: involuntary resonance.

cards.power: The Cuddle Hormone: Heal a fractured Stage or lower the Quest Die by 1.
cards.lore: Increases trust, reduces fear. Warning: Can cause aggression against 'outsiders'.
cards.gradeReason: The warning on the lore is the whole card — it names the cost of in-group bonding, making this the most honest card in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: soft science textbook illustration. Subject: golden blob hugging a rock, warm light emanating, a shadow at the edge of frame. Mood: conditional warmth.

cards.power: Calm Down: Reset the Quest Die to 3.
cards.lore: The wandering nerve of compassion. Stimulate for peace.
cards.gradeReason: Die reset to 3 is clean utility but requires no performance and generates no theatre.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anatomical diagram. Subject: electric eel threaded through a human silhouette, all organs lit up in sequence. Mood: systemic calm.

cards.power: Social Reject: Inflict 'Damage' on an Actor who is ignored.
cards.lore: Social rejection activates the same brain regions as physical pain. (Ref: Lieberman)
cards.gradeReason: Forces the table to actively choose to ignore someone, then punishes that choice — the mechanic makes the research land in real time.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: neuroscience watercolor. Subject: porcupine with bandages covering both physical quills and invisible wounds, scanning the room. Mood: documented hurt.

cards.power: Leviathan: Impose strict order. No other player may speak this turn.
cards.lore: "Life is nasty, brutish, and short. War of all against all."
cards.gradeReason: Silencing all other players in one move is the Leviathan — the table feels exactly what Hobbes prescribed and resents it immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political philosophy engraving. Subject: bulldog in a padlocked kennel labeled KEEP OUT, no one else visible, chain across the whole yard. Mood: enforced order.

cards.power: Natural Goodness: Remove a 'Corruption' or 'Civilization' effect.
cards.lore: "Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains."
cards.gradeReason: Removing a Corruption effect is correct but depends on those effect types being in play — against Hobbes it's explosive, alone it's inert.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Romantic landscape illustration. Subject: stag in an ancient forest, chains dissolving in the sunlight, butterflies landing on the broken links. Mood: recovered freedom.

cards.power: Humankind: Re-roll the die if the result was cynical/negative.
cards.lore: "Most people, deep down, are pretty decent." (Ref: Im Grunde gut)
cards.gradeReason: Forces the table to categorize a die result as 'cynical' before re-rolling — that judgment is where all the real action happens.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: optimistic editorial illustration. Subject: golden retriever with a tennis ball, children playing in background, a scoreboard showing improving results. Mood: evidence-based hope.

cards.power: Fiction Trap: Create a false conflict.
cards.lore: "A story we tell ourselves. Real kids on islands cooperated. (Ref: Golding vs. Reality)"
cards.gradeReason: Introducing a conflict the table knows to be fictional — and watching how they respond anyway — is the Kayfabizarro project in one card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: horror parody. Subject: pig's head in glasses labeled CIVILIZATION ENDS HERE, small figure in background actually building something. Mood: manufactured chaos.

cards.power: Pointing: Reveal a hidden card from another player's hand.
cards.lore: "We cooperate to survive. Shared Intentionality. (Ref: Why We Cooperate)"
cards.gradeReason: Hand reveal as 'pointing' is clean conceptually but is a common mechanic — shared intentionality deserves a two-player trigger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: primatology fieldwork illustration. Subject: chimpanzee pointing at a concealed card, human researcher looking where the finger leads. Mood: cross-species disclosure.

cards.power: Joint Effort: Works only if another player helps. Effect is doubled.
cards.lore: "I can't catch the stag alone. If I chase the rabbit, we both lose."
cards.gradeReason: A power that literally only activates through cooperation makes the table's social dynamics the mechanical condition — no other card does this.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: game theory diagram illustration. Subject: two beavers lifting a log together, a lone rabbit watching from the side, a stag visible in the distance. Mood: conditional reward.

cards.power: Exploit: Steal the benefit of the previous player's action.
cards.lore: The fear of being suckered. The reason we invented punishment.
cards.gradeReason: Reactive benefit-theft rewires the social contract retroactively — the previous player will remember this, and the table will track who plays it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nest observation illustration. Subject: large bird occupying a nest built by others, wearing a tiny flag reading MINE, ants watching. Mood: parasitic comfort.

cards.power: Elinor Ostrom: All players draw 1 card.
cards.lore: What we share grows, unless we believe the tragedy myth. (Ref: Ostrom)
cards.gradeReason: Mass card draw named after a Nobel laureate — Ostrom's insight deserves a conditional mechanic, not flat resource distribution.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pastoral watercolor. Subject: flock of sheep on shared land all growing larger simultaneously, a small locked gate unused in the corner. Mood: managed abundance.

cards.power: Reconciliation: Restore peace after a conflict scene.
cards.lore: "Empathy is biological, not a choice. The Age of Empathy."
cards.gradeReason: Post-conflict peace restoration is correct and needed but is the quietest card on its page — chimpanzee reconciliation data deserves more theatre.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: primatology watercolor. Subject: two chimpanzees, one offering a banana after a fight, the other still deciding. Mood: biological generosity.

cards.power: CEO Status: Ignore the negative consequences of a decision.
cards.lore: "1% of people. 4% of CEOs. They know the lyrics but not the music."
cards.gradeReason: 'They know the lyrics but not the music' is the sharpest lore line in the deck — and a card that ignores its own consequences is every table's villain.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate horror portrait. Subject: shark in a pinstripe suit smiling at a graph going straight up while the office below floods. Mood: undisturbed consequence.

cards.power: Vibe Check: Change the mood of the Stage to match your Actor.
cards.lore: "We catch feelings faster than viruses. (Ref: Christakis)"
cards.gradeReason: Stage-mood alignment through declared Actor state is both a mechanic and a theory of mind enacted — whoever plays this controls the emotional weather.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: infectious biology illustration. Subject: hippo yawning, all surrounding animals mid-yawn, birds already airborne mid-yawn. Mood: compulsory resonance.

cards.power: Cynicism: Negate a "Good" act.
cards.lore: "The myth that civilization is just a thin layer over a beast. BLÖDSINN!"
cards.gradeReason: A card that negates Good acts and is simultaneously called BLÖDSINN on its own face — playing it proves the lore right about cynicism.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cracked mask illustration. Subject: pristine white mask with face-muscle visible through spreading cracks, question mark on the wall behind it. Mood: self-defeating argument.

cards.power: Rational Fool: Make a decision that benefits only you, lose 1 Friend.
cards.lore: A rational utility maximizer who doesn't exist. (Ref: Game Theory)
cards.gradeReason: The power enforces the very behavioral assumption the lore declares false — playing it correctly proves you are the fiction.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: economic satire diagram. Subject: robot with a calculator chest and a missing heart cavity, pointing at a utility curve going nowhere useful. Mood: optimized emptiness.

cards.power: Echo Chamber: Ignore any card played by a 'Different' species.
cards.lore: We only see what the algorithm wants us to see. (Ref: Pariser)
cards.gradeReason: Mechanically blocking input from any Different species makes the table experience the bubble — whoever plays this will immediately see what they miss.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: aquarium diagram. Subject: goldfish in a VR headset, a larger world visible outside the bowl, the fish reading DIFFERENT on everything outside. Mood: curated blindness.

cards.power: Health Hazard: -1 to Quest Die.
cards.lore: As deadly as 15 cigarettes a day. A biological warning signal.
cards.gradeReason: Die reduction is the most passive power for the strongest public health data point in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: arctic documentary illustration. Subject: penguin alone on a shrinking ice floe, a heart icon in a thought bubble, no other figures visible. Mood: documented isolation.

cards.power: Scroll Doom: Skip your turn to draw a card.
cards.lore: We are alone together. Connection without demand. (Ref: Turkle)
cards.gradeReason: Skipping your social turn to gain a resource is Scroll Doom mechanically enacted — the trade looks attractive and is described perfectly by the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: soft horror illustration. Subject: squirrel holding a phone, acorns unpicked around it, a perfect autumn scene it is not seeing. Mood: absent presence.

cards.power: Flow State: Play an extra card if it fits the story perfectly.
cards.lore: Doing it because you love it. Rewards can kill this. (Ref: Deci & Ryan)
cards.gradeReason: Bonus card on perfect story fit is the right mechanic but 'perfectly' is a judgment call that will produce table disputes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: expressionist illustration. Subject: cat chasing a laser dot with absolute commitment, no audience, no prize, pure trajectory. Mood: unconditional engagement.

cards.power: Synergy: +1 to Quest Die for every player who helps.
cards.lore: We are designed to work together. (Ref: Sennett)
cards.gradeReason: Scalable die bonus for collective help is mechanically satisfying but needs The Stag Hunt or The Commons in play to fully sing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: biological colony diagram. Subject: ants building a bridge from their own bodies, the die above visible through the gap they're crossing. Mood: structural cooperation.

cards.power: Resignation: Discard a card to do nothing.
cards.lore: Work that serves no purpose. Soul-destroying. (Ref: Graeber)
cards.gradeReason: The only card in the corpus that spends a resource to perform absence — the table will feel the pointlessness in real time.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: office satire watercolor. Subject: hamster in a suit feeding documents into a shredder, the shredder outputting identical documents. Mood: productive futility.

cards.power: Choice Arch: Influence the next player's decision without forcing them.
cards.lore: Small changes in context can change behavior. (Ref: Thaler)
cards.gradeReason: Influence-without-force is one of the most interesting concepts in the deck but the execution method is left entirely to the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: behavioral economics illustration. Subject: baby elephant following a larger one down a path with subtle arrows embedded in the ground. Mood: gentle determinism.

cards.power: Touch: Connect two separated cards.
cards.lore: We cannot live without touch. The skin is our social organ. (Ref: Grunwald)
cards.gradeReason: Bridging two separated cards is physically simple but conceptually rich — the definition of 'separated' needs table agreement.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tactile science illustration. Subject: mole touching a page, golden warmth spreading from each fingertip to nearby objects. Mood: contact as knowledge.

cards.power: Hartmut Rosa: Amplify the current 'Vibe'.
cards.lore: When the world answers us. Not echo, but answer.
cards.gradeReason: Amplifying an existing Vibe is correct but 'current Vibe' is undefined without Emotional Contagion having set one first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: acoustic physics illustration. Subject: two bats hanging close, sound waves visibly synchronizing between them, a fly between them unaware. Mood: frequency found.

cards.power: Desperation: Force a connection (play a card on top of another).
cards.lore: A biological deficit. We wither without contact.
cards.gradeReason: Forcing a card connection through desperation rather than choice makes the touch mechanic urgent and slightly uncomfortable — exactly the phenomenology.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: clinical illustration. Subject: sphinx cat wrapped entirely in a blanket, one paw touching a nearby object for warmth, no other creatures present. Mood: biological necessity.

cards.power: Immersion: The Quest Die cannot be tipped this turn.
cards.lore: Total absorption. The ego dissolves. (Ref: Csikszentmihalyi)
cards.gradeReason: Quest Die immunity through immersion is the experience of flow made structural — the session stabilizes without the player needing to defend anything.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fluid motion illustration. Subject: otter mid-wave, completely absorbed, the wave and the otter indistinguishable from each other. Mood: dissolved attention.

cards.power: Missed Shot: Negate an attack or aggressive move.
cards.lore: Most soldiers didn't shoot to kill. We are not natural killers. (Ref: Marshall)
cards.gradeReason: Names our inbuilt hesitation and makes it a game mechanic — aggression is negated not by force but by the body's own refusal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: war documentary illustration. Subject: soldier ant with a rifle aimed at nothing in particular, hand trembling, the target outside the frame. Mood: involuntary mercy.

cards.power: Ceasefire: Pause the Quest Die for one round.
cards.lore: When the propaganda failed, they played football. 1914.
cards.gradeReason: Pausing the Die for exactly one round before everything resumes is historically exact and emotionally precise — the table knows it won't last.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sepia documentary watercolor. Subject: German shepherd and poodle playing football in a muddy field, barbed wire visible at the edge of the image. Mood: temporary sanity.

cards.power: Dehumanize: Turn a 'Friend' card into an 'Enemy'.
cards.lore: We need to be lied to in order to kill. (Ref: Bernays)
cards.gradeReason: Flipping a Friend card to Enemy with no other mechanic is the cleanest demonstration of how propaganda works — and the table will feel it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wartime parrot poster. Subject: macaw screaming MONSTERS! through a megaphone at a figure who was just helping someone a moment ago. Mood: manufactured enmity.

cards.power: Civil Disobedience: Stop the game flow to change a rule.
cards.lore: Power comes from obedience. Withdraw it. (Ref: Gandhi)
cards.gradeReason: A card that stops the game to change a rule doesn't operate within the game — it operates ON it. Most structurally radical mechanic in the corpus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political protest illustration. Subject: goat sitting calmly in front of a tank that has stopped, a daisy held up, game pieces visible scattered around. Mood: principled obstruction.

cards.power: Debunk: Remove a 'Leader' status.
cards.lore: Real alphas are caretakers, not bullies. (Ref: Mech)
cards.gradeReason: Status removal is mechanically functional but the power name 'Debunk' does editorial commentary — the card should make the Leader prove themselves instead.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wildlife documentary parody. Subject: wolf labeled ALPHA on a chart with downward arrows, a smaller wolf quietly distributing food to the group. Mood: empirical correction.

cards.power: Ridicule: The player with the most cards must discard one.
cards.lore: Cutting down the tall poppy. Keeping egos in check. (Ref: Boehm)
cards.gradeReason: Automatically targeting the richest hand with enforced discard is the egalitarian impulse made mechanical — no coalition required, the rule does it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: behavioral ecology illustration. Subject: mob of meerkats standing around the highest individual, all pointing down with one paw each. Mood: collective calibration.

cards.power: Brain Damage: Gain power, but lose Empathy (cannot assist others).
cards.lore: Power causes brain damage. It shuts down mirror neurons. (Ref: Keltner)
cards.gradeReason: Gain-power-lose-empathy is the most precise trade in the deck — the card self-enforces its own thesis by preventing the player from helping anyone afterward.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark political cartoon. Subject: toad in a chair, growing larger, brain visible outside its head shrinking as the chair expands. Mood: neurological trade-off.

cards.power: Round Table: Everyone draws a card.
cards.lore: For 95% of human history, we lived as equals. (Ref: Graeber/Wengrow)
cards.gradeReason: Mass card draw — the lore carries 300,000 years of evidence and the power delivers single-round resource parity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: circular diagram. Subject: fish arranged in a perfect ring around a small glowing table, each one receiving exactly one item, perfectly symmetrical. Mood: structural fairness.

cards.power: Innate Goodness: Aid another player freely.
cards.lore: We help before we can talk. It's not taught, it's there. (Ref: Warneken)
cards.gradeReason: Unconditional free aid with no catch, no trade, no mechanic tax — which makes it feel almost suspicious at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: developmental psychology illustration. Subject: small puppy bringing keys to a larger dog who can't reach them, no context required. Mood: pre-verbal generosity.

cards.power: It Takes A Village: Use another player's Skill/Power.
cards.lore: Mothers and Others. We share the burden. (Ref: Hrdy)
cards.gradeReason: Borrowing another player's power is cooperative but needs the other player's consent protocol to be fully resolved.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: marsupial family illustration. Subject: kangaroo with two joeys — one hers, one a neighbor's — all three equally tended. Mood: distributed parenthood.

cards.power: Reset: Clear the Stage (it was just a game).
cards.lore: Play is the foundation of culture. It requires trust. (Ref: Huizinga)
cards.gradeReason: 'It was just a game' as the parenthetical justification for a total Stage reset is the most philosophically honest Kayfabizarro power ever written.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: folk play illustration. Subject: two foxes tumbling together in grass, the same posture that would be a fight, clearly not one. Mood: trust enacted.

cards.power: Schooling: Force a card to conform to a specific suit/color.
cards.lore: We are taught to compete. We are molded. (Ref: Kohn)
cards.gradeReason: Forcing card conformity is mechanically correct but forcing a player's narration to conform would hit harder than a card attribute.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grooming parody illustration. Subject: poodle on a table being clipped into a shape it didn't choose, watching another dog running free through a window. Mood: applied standardization.

cards.power: Categorical Imperative: Establish a Universal Rule for the game.
cards.lore: "The starry sky above me, the moral law within me."
cards.gradeReason: A card that legislates a new game rule for everyone is the Categorical Imperative with teeth — the table must now live under whatever rule Kant declared.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Starry Night homage. Subject: stork standing at a moral compass, writing a new rule on a scroll under a vast night sky. Mood: universal obligation.

cards.power: To Be: Immunize an Actor against material loss.
cards.lore: "To Have or To Be? That is the question of sanity."
cards.gradeReason: Material-loss immunity is the right mechanic but 'material loss' is undefined in core Kayfabizarro — the lore's existential clarity outpaces the power.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: humanist philosophy illustration. Subject: owl holding both a withered plant and a growing one, the growing one untouchable behind a soft glow. Mood: chosen existence.

cards.power: I and Thou: Create an unbreakable bond between two Actors.
cards.lore: "All real living is meeting. No 'It', only 'Thou.'"
cards.gradeReason: An unbreakable two-Actor bond is the only card in the deck that creates a permanent relational category — the table is changed after it is played.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: connection portrait. Subject: two horses face to face, a glowing thread between their foreheads, geometry of encounter visible. Mood: irreversible recognition.

cards.power: Action: Start a new narrative thread (Quest).
cards.lore: "The banality of evil. But also the power of beginning."
cards.gradeReason: Arendt's 'natality' as a Quest trigger — the right to begin is the most underrated power in politics and the most optimistic card in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: typewriter documentary illustration. Subject: fox at a typewriter, a new blank page rolling in, previous pages crumpled but visible. Mood: deliberate beginning.

cards.power: Incremental Gain: +1 to the Die roll.
cards.lore: Not Utopia. Just a little bit better than yesterday. (Ref: Kevin Kelly)
cards.gradeReason: '+1 to the Die roll' — correct philosophy, minimal mechanics, no performance required or produced.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ant colony illustration. Subject: ants building incrementally — a slightly higher structure than yesterday, measured with a tiny ruler. Mood: sustainable progress.

cards.power: Find the Others: Unite all players against the Quest.
cards.lore: Being human is a team sport. (Ref: Douglas Rushkoff)
cards.gradeReason: Uniting all players against the shared Quest is the cooperative endgame mechanic the deck has been building toward — it only works if the session earned it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ensemble illustration. Subject: cat, dog, bird, and mouse all placing paws/claws/wings on the same point simultaneously. Mood: convergent purpose.

cards.power: Manifest: If you say it happens, it happens.
cards.lore: If we believe we are selfish, we become selfish. Change the story.
cards.gradeReason: Performative speech as a game mechanic — your credibility IS your power, the table must accept what you declare.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chameleon color-theory illustration. Subject: chameleon speaking a color, turning that color, changing the branch beneath it. Mood: stated reality.

cards.power: The Verb: Restart the game if you lose.
cards.lore: Hope is a verb with its sleeves rolled up. (Ref: Solnit/Orr)
cards.gradeReason: Restart-on-loss is the most emotionally serious mechanic in the corpus — losing is not the end, and the table has to decide whether they believe it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rocket pigeon illustration. Subject: white pigeon with a rocket pack lifting off from the ground, wings already working even before the engines fire. Mood: active continuation.

cards.power: Interrupt: Cancel the last action. Shout 'BlödsInn!'
cards.lore: When the story gets boring or fake, hit the reset button.
cards.gradeReason: The interrupt that names itself as the game's quality-control mechanism — available as a card, so you can hold it and time the detonation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic horror cartoon. Subject: wild-haired figure slamming a pie into a bureaucratic certificate while shouting upward. Mood: principled interruption.

cards.power: The Work: Treat the game as real. Overact your next turn.
cards.lore: It's fake, but the emotion is real. That's the point.
cards.gradeReason: A card named after the game that instructs you to treat the game as real — and 'overact' is the only correct instruction it could give.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: luchador portrait. Subject: wrestling mask with many faces beneath it, each layer more expressive than the last. Mood: sincere performance.

cards.power: Cut: Physically cut a card in half to destroy it forever.
cards.lore: The ultimate tool of the DIY anarchist.
cards.gradeReason: The only card in the corpus that requires physical destruction of another card — you cannot take this action back, making it the most final power in the game.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anarchist zine illustration. Subject: scissors with eyes cutting through a rulebook, cards visible on either side of the cut. Mood: irreversible liberation.

cards.power: Mashup: Stick two cards together permanently.
cards.lore: Make connections where there are none.
cards.gradeReason: The Scissors destroy permanently; The Glue Stick connects permanently — together they are the deck's creation and destruction pair, both requiring physical commitment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: collage art. Subject: two unrelated cards being pressed together, new meaning leaking from the join. Mood: productive accident.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: HILFE, ICH BIN EIN MENSCH! – The Source Deck Where the Science Fights Back (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Most card games hand you a rulebook and ask you to behave. This one hands you a pair of scissors and dares you to cut the rule you disagree with in half.

Watch a single round and you stop asking what it teaches. Someone plays The Stag Hunt and it does nothing at all, dead weight on the table, until a second player agrees out loud to hunt with them, and only then does it pay double. Someone else lays down Non-Violent Resistance, the whole game stops, and the room has to rewrite a rule before anyone moves again. Then a hand reaches for The Scissors and a card gets cut in two and is gone for the rest of the night, no take-backs. Cooperation, civil disobedience, and irreversible loss are not printed here as facts you nod along to. They are moves you have to make in front of other people.

This is the source deck, the one the entire Kayfabizarro project grew out of: 56 cut-and-play cards that take evolutionary psychology, social neuroscience, and the philosophy of cooperation off the reading list and put them in your hands as things you perform out loud while the table rules on whether they hold. Social Story Wrestling, in the original recipe.
